title: Microsoft Azure Hybrid Cloud
description: Connect office systems and online apps with one staff sign-in. A useful example for a business that already uses Microsoft tools.
steps: Staff sign in with access checks.
Link the office network to Azure.
Host business apps and their data.
Track health and restore lost data.
note: Confirm where apps, data and backups will be stored. Plan private connections where needed, and keep testing separate from live business work.

title: AWS Customer App Platform
description: Run a customer portal, booking service or business app that can handle busy and quiet periods.
steps: Filter and deliver incoming web traffic.
Keep app records and uploaded files.
note: Plan for a server or location failure. Protect database access and passwords, monitor the service and test restoring backups.

title: Google Cloud Serverless Apps
description: Run online forms, booking services and business tools without managing the application servers yourself.
steps: Route requests and apply access rules.
Run an API in managed containers.
Process background work and track health.
note: Set limits on running services and costs. Check database connections and whether each service is available in the required location.

title: Private Cloud with OpenShift
description: Run business apps on your own systems or an approved cloud when you need control over where they run.
steps: Provide the compute and storage base.
note: Plan who supports the platform, installs updates and manages storage. Keep and test a separate recovery setup.

title: React and Node.js Web Apps
description: Build a customer portal, booking tool or staff dashboard with screens and features that fit your work.
steps: Store records and cache frequent reads.
note: Check permissions and incoming data in the service that runs the business rules. Add extra tools only when there is a clear need.

title: .NET Business Systems
description: Build staff portals and business software that connect with the Microsoft systems you already use.
note: Check database compatibility, licence costs and recovery needs. Keep application access separate from database administration.

title: Java and Spring Business Apps
description: Build business software for orders, customer services and connections to larger or older systems.
note: Start with a system your team can support. Separate it into smaller services only when scale or team responsibilities require it.

title: WordPress and WooCommerce
description: Set up a product catalogue or online store where your team can manage products, content and orders.
steps: Deliver store pages and filter traffic.
Store orders, media and catalogue data.
Send payment processing to a provider.
note: Use supported add-ons, protect administrator access and test updates and backups. Use a payment provider to handle card payments.

title: SAP and Business Integration
description: Connect SAP accounts, orders and stock information to other business tools, so teams do less copying between systems.
steps: Map and validate approved API messages.
note: Use supported SAP connections. Check licences, prevent duplicate updates and keep a record of failed actions. Avoid direct changes to ERP database tables.

title: Oracle Business Data Integration
description: Use information from your Oracle systems in new business apps and reports while keeping the main system in place.
steps: Serve apps without overloading the core.
note: Check the supported way to connect to each Oracle product. Confirm software versions, licences and the effect of data copying on the live system.

title: Salesforce Sales and Service
description: Keep customer enquiries, sales follow-ups and service requests connected to orders and accounts.
steps: Capture a lead or service request.
Send approved orders and status updates.
note: Agree which system keeps the main customer record. Check access permissions, connection limits and how failed or duplicate updates are handled.

title: Workflow Automation with n8n
description: Move requests, invoice follow-ups and approvals between tools, using steps your team has agreed.
steps: Receive a request or system event.
Validate inputs and connect approved tools.
Pause important actions for a decision.
Record the outcome and failed tasks.
note: Protect connection passwords and check incoming requests. Make sure a failed step can be retried without creating the same action twice.

title: Cloud Data Warehouse
description: Bring sales, accounts and operations data together so teams can work from the same business numbers.
steps: Clean, test and organise reporting tables.
note: Agree who owns each source, how often data is updated and how the numbers are checked. Set access and usage limits.

title: Spark Data Lakehouse
description: Organise large files and years of business records for reporting, analysis and AI projects.
steps: Land approved data in object storage.
Serve governed analysis and model inputs.
note: Keep a list of data sources and owners. Set access, storage and cost limits, and decide when old records should be removed.

title: Kafka Event Processing
description: Share updates about orders, stock and payment status between systems as the work happens.
steps: Update views and notify other systems.
note: Agree the message format and order. Check delayed updates and make sure replaying a message does not repeat a business action.

title: Practical Business Dashboards
description: Bring sales and daily work into clear reports without starting with a large data system.
steps: Collect data on an agreed schedule.
Keep reporting separate from live apps.
note: Use read-only access for reports. Agree what each number means and show when the data was last updated. Expand the setup only when needed.

title: Private Document Assistant
description: Help staff find answers in approved company documents, using an AI model running on your own systems.
steps: Find relevant content the user may access.
Generate an answer using retrieved sources.
Show evidence and flag uncertain answers.
note: Check hardware needs, document permissions and answer quality. Show sources. An AI answer still needs checking and may be wrong.

title: Azure Document AI Assistant
description: Help staff search company documents and prepare answers using Microsoft cloud AI, with access checks and sources.
steps: Verify the user and their permissions.
Create a response using retrieved content.
Check quality and retain approved logs.
note: Check model availability, data handling terms and the location used for processing. Test that people see only documents they are allowed to access.

title: Google Cloud AI Applications
description: Add document search and AI support to staff or customer apps using Google Cloud services.
steps: Find relevant content with access filters.
Show sources, collect feedback and logs.
note: Check answer quality, document access, data handling and service availability in the required location before giving users access.

title: Prediction and ML Serving
description: Use business data to test tools such as demand forecasts or image checks, and track how well they work.
steps: Validate inputs and separate test data.
Train and evaluate a suitable model.
note: Compare results with a simple existing method. Track errors and changes in accuracy, and keep a way to return to the previous model.

title: Infrastructure and GitOps Delivery
description: Set up systems and release software through reviewed, repeatable steps, with a way to recover if a change goes wrong.
steps: Apply reviewed app changes to Kubernetes.
note: Protect deployment access and stored settings. Separate testing from live systems and plan how software and database changes can be reversed.

title: Monitoring and Service Health
description: Bring faults, slow apps and system alerts into one place so the right team can investigate.
steps: Store metrics, logs and traces separately.
note: Agree useful alerts and who responds to them. Keep private information out of logs and set limits on how much monitoring data is stored.

title: Identity and Secure App Access
description: Give staff one way to sign in to business apps, with extra sign-in checks and clear access permissions.
steps: Verify tokens and enforce app permissions.
note: One sign-in does not cover every security need. Also check devices, network access, administrator accounts and emergency account recovery.

title: Backup and Recovery Foundation
description: Back up important business systems and practise restoring them, so the team knows what to do after a failure.
steps: Identify business systems and recovery order.
Capture consistent backups and transaction logs.
Keep an isolated, immutable copy where supported.
Rebuild systems and verify restored data.
note: Agree how quickly systems must return and how much recent data could be lost. Keep a separate protected copy and practise a full restore.
